LMP.eli5: The cost of serving the next megawatt of electricity at a specific location, combining energy cost, transmission line congestion, and power line losses.
LMP.technical: Calculated by Security-Constrained Economic Dispatch (SCED) as: LMP = Energy Component (MEC) + Congestion Component (MCC) + Marginal Loss Component (MLC).

CONE.eli5: The estimated annual cost to build and operate a brand-new natural gas peaker plant in MISO, used as the benchmark price cap in capacity auctions.
CONE.technical: Determined annually per Local Resource Zone (LRZ) under Tariff Module E-1 to establish the maximum clearing price in the Planning Resource Auction (PRA).

PRA.eli5: MISO's annual capacity auction where utilities ensure they have enough power plants reserved to keep the lights on during peak summer and winter days.
PRA.technical: Annual auction conducted under Tariff Module E-1 enforcing Planning Reserve Margin Requirements (PRMR) across all 10 MISO Local Resource Zones.

MTEP.eli5: MISO's comprehensive multi-billion dollar master plan to build, upgrade, and reinforce high-voltage power lines across 15 states.
MTEP.technical: Annual planning cycle approved by the MISO Board of Directors containing baseline reliability, market efficiency, and public policy transmission projects.

LRTP.eli5: A multi-tranche regional superhighway transmission initiative to transport low-cost wind and solar from rural areas to major cities.
LRTP.technical: Strategic 20-year planning horizon (Tranche 1 approved at $10.3B / 3,600+ miles; Tranche 2 covering MISO Midwest; Tranche 3 covering MISO South).

JTIQ.eli5: A partnership between MISO and Southwest Power Pool (SPP) to unlock new power lines right along their shared border.
JTIQ.technical: Coordinated seam transmission study between MISO and SPP identifying high-priority interregional projects to lower interconnection network upgrade costs.

DPP.eli5: The rigorous technical study phase where power plant developers wait for MISO approval to connect their new wind, solar, or battery project to the grid.
DPP.technical: Three-phase cluster study process (DPP Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3) evaluating system impact, thermal constraints, and network upgrade cost assignments.

LOLE.eli5: A strict safety standard requiring that the electric grid has enough generators so power never runs short more than 1 day in 10 years.
LOLE.technical: Probabilistic resource adequacy metric standard targeting an LOLE of less than 0.1 days/year (1 day in 10 years) used to calibrate the Planning Reserve Margin.

OASIS.eli5: The public website and database where power companies reserve and purchase capacity on MISO's high-voltage lines.
OASIS.technical: FERC-mandated real-time information and reservation system (Order 889) for booking Available Transfer Capability (ATC) and transmission services.

FTR.eli5: A financial contract that protects electricity buyers and sellers from unexpected price spikes caused by crowded power lines.
FTR.technical: Financial instruments that entitle the holder to a revenue stream or charge based on the Day-Ahead Market Locational Marginal Price congestion component differences.
